20.0.2.en: "The labourers": they are all people whom God calls to live with Him and to serve Him.

20.1.0.en: It is God who went out, that is, He is the One who takes the initiative in seeking man, and who begins with love, and He went out at dawn, at the first hour, seeking the hearts of His children.

20.1.1.en: The well-known Jewish hours are five, which signify the life of man, and they are (noting that the hour here is not 60 minutes, but a period of time extending to the hour that follows it):

20.1.7.en: These hours also point to the history of mankind: Adam, then Noah, then Abraham, then Moses and the prophets, then Christ.

20.1.8.en: And the meaning of this is that God seeks man throughout the history of mankind, and throughout his life, that perhaps he will respond and be saved.

20.2.0.en: "Even": it is the end of life, and the Day of Judgment.

20.2.2.en: "Those hired about the eleventh hour": when the lord reproached them for standing idle all the day, they said: "Because no man hath hired us" (v. 7), that is, they did not understand the call of God, so they remained without spiritual work all their lives, until they took notice at the end of life.

20.2.3.en: "A penny": it is salvation and eternal life.

20.2.4.en: So everyone, as long as he has believed in Christ and worked with Him even for one hour, receives eternal life. But one differs from another in the measure of his enjoyment, fellowship and attachment to God.

20.2.5.en: It may be that the call came at the end of life, and the person responded to it with all his heart, and so becomes like those of the first hour, indeed he may be better than they in proportion to his love for God.

20.2.6.en: And if someone says, I will wait until the eleventh hour, since salvation is given to all, and I do not want to be distinguished in the Kingdom of Heaven, this means:

20.2.7.en: First: that he does not know that his life may end at any moment.

20.2.8.en: Second: that he does not appreciate the value of fellowship with God and His love, and so he belittles his relationship with God on earth.

20.3.0.en: Those of the first hour signify the Jews, who thought that salvation was limited to them and not for the Gentiles, and that if non-Jews believed in Christ, they would be of a lower rank than the Jews who became Christians, and they spoke of those of the eleventh hour, saying: "These last"... But Christ spoke to them with love, saying: "Friend".

20.3.1.en: And in this murmuring was an interference in the work of God as Judge, for He gave each one what He had agreed with him, and then showed grace to another, without diminishing anything from the Jew or the murmurer.

20.3.2.en: "Thine eye evil": that is, selfish, thinking of good for yourself and refusing it for others, and envying others for what they receive.

20.3.3.en: "Many be called": God seeks the salvation of all. But only a few believe and live in love, and these alone are saved.

20.3.4.en: In sum, Christ gives salvation to everyone who believes in Him and lives with Him in His Church, whether he lived a life of repentance from the beginning of his life, or at the end of his days.

20.3.5.en: And this does not deny the existence of mansions and degrees in the Kingdom, but the talk here is only about entering the Kingdom.

20.3.6.en: Look at all people as the image of God, and that they may precede you into the Kingdom, and do good to everyone, especially to the weak and those far from God, that perhaps they will repent, knowing that they may increase in the love of God more than you.

20.4.0.en: "Then": after Christ's words about His coming sufferings.

20.4.1.en: "The mother of Zebedee's children": she is Salome, and her coming forward was at the urging of her two sons, so that she would support them in their request to Christ, and the proof of that is that Christ addressed the two of them afterward, and not the mother.

20.4.2.en: "A certain thing": out of courtesy on her part, and her sense of the difficulty of what she was asking and that it might be refused, she said to Him: I desire a certain thing of thee.

20.4.3.en: "What wilt thou?": Christ knew what she wanted, but He intended that she review herself one last time about what she would ask.

20.4.4.en: The mother of Zebedee's children came to Christ with her two sons, and worshiped Him in faith, and since she thought that Christ would have an earthly kingdom, as the rest of the Jews think, then out of love for her two sons she asked Him that they would have a distinguished place in this kingdom above the rest of the disciples, so that they would sit, one on His right hand and the other on His left, that is, that they would have chief place over the others.

20.5.0.en: Christ directed the attention of the two disciples to the sufferings that must be endured in order to reach the Kingdom, which takes place throughout life, to turn their eyes away from attachment to earthly positions, and to think in a spiritual way of the Kingdom of Heaven as love and fellowship with God, and not a search for positions or chief place. And He asked them a clear question: are you able to drink of the cup of sufferings and be baptized with the baptism of death? And they answered without deliberation and understanding and said: "We are able." And here Christ directed their attention to the fact that being in the Kingdom is a grace from God, so a person cannot by his will alone endure sufferings for the sake of Christ, but by the help of God.

20.5.1.en: "It is prepared of my Father": that is, for those who have completed their striving, and so deserve the grace of God. And although the will of the Son and the Father is one will, He said here "my Father", to raise their thinking from the earthly kingship with Him to the heavenly Kingdom, that is, with the Father.

20.6.0.en: The love of greatness stirred in the hearts of the disciples when they heard the desire of the two sons of Zebedee, James and John, for this chief place, and they were angered and troubled, for they feared that the two would obtain what they asked.

20.7.0.en: Christ warned them that striving for chief place is the thinking of the people of the world, and not of the children of God. And He declared clearly the importance of striving for humility in the form of serving one another, and each one's submission to the other, for this is what makes them great in the sight of God, and gives them a distinguished standing in heaven. That is, the world strives for chief place and domination, but the children of God for humility and service.

20.8.0.en: Christ gave Himself as an example of humility, for He did not seek a worldly position in which many would serve Him, but came to be a servant of mankind, and to die for it to redeem it.

20.8.1.en: Do you look for what service you can offer to others, and how to submit to them, or for your own standing and dignity among them? May you from today submit to all, to be raised in the sight of God.

20.9.s.en: (4) The opening of the eyes of the two blind men

20.9.0.en: This is the last miracle that Christ performs before entering Jerusalem. As He was walking on the way with the multitude, there were two blind men sitting by the way, who seem to have been begging. When they heard the voice of the multitude, and learned that this was the procession of Christ who heals the sick, they believed in His power to heal, and cried out asking Him for that, confident that He is the awaited Messiah, the son of David.

20.9.1.en: Two blind men are mentioned here, whereas Mark and Luke mention one blind man, who seems to have been the one who spoke more than the second (Mk 10:46-52; Lk 18:35-43).

20.10.0.en: By their much crying out they troubled the multitude, who tried to silence them so that they could enjoy listening to the words of Christ, but they kept crying out with insistence, declaring their faith and their great need of healing, seizing this opportunity that could not be replaced.

20.10.1.en: Press on God in asking, for this shows the extent of your faith, and do not be hindered by the thoughts of people that keep you from God.

20.11.0.en: Jesus stood still and called the two blind men, for He cares greatly for the one who seeks Him, although He waits a little, to show the extent of his clinging and persistence in prayer. Then He asked them what they wanted, that they might show their need of healing, and they declared it. And then His tenderness appeared and He healed them. And from the excess of their joy, they followed Him, to enjoy like the others listening to His teachings and seeing His miracles.

20.11.1.en: God is ready to grant you spiritual insight, that is, discernment and understanding, if you ask for them with persistence, for His tenderness toward you is unlimited. And if He grants you wisdom and discernment, follow Christ in all your steps so that your faith is not theoretical, but you enjoy fellowship with Him every day more than before.

20.11.2.en: Christ's entry into Jerusalem, the parable of the husbandmen

21.0.0.en: From this chapter begin the events that took place in the last week of the life of Christ on earth. And the Holy Bible mentions them in detail, because they concern the accomplishment of salvation for the whole world. Christ drew near to Jerusalem (on the morning of Sunday), and to the village of Bethphage, which lies east of it at the Mount of Olives. So He sent two of His disciples, saying to them: when you enter the city, you will find an ass (a female donkey) and a colt (the young donkey), so loose them from their tying, and if anyone objects to you, say, The Lord hath need of them, and he will let them go with you.

21.0.1.en: And this was by divine arrangement, or the owners of the ass and the colt were informed, in a way not mentioned in the Holy Bible, that two would come asking for them for the Lord, and so they gave them to them.

21.0.2.en: "An ass ... and a colt": they signify people, that is, the Jews and the Gentiles, who have become as dull as the donkey because of their distance from God, whether by material preoccupation or by the worship of idols.

21.0.3.en: And see how great was the humility of Christ, who says that He has need of them, although He is the Creator of everything!

21.0.4.en: And thus He shows His need of the souls of His children, that they may return to Him and live with Him.

21.0.5.en: He is the giver of all gifts and perfect in Himself, but it is His love and humility that make Him ask.

21.0.6.en: And see the tenderness of God riding on the colt, but, so as not to tire the colt, He also rides on the ass a little, then on the colt a little, for He has compassion on His creation, and how much more on mankind.

21.0.7.en: And no one had ever ridden the colt, and this signifies not being subject except to God.

21.0.8.en: And He gave authority to the two disciples, that is, the priests of the New Testament, to loose mankind from its bonds, and this is the authority of loosing and binding in the sacrament of confession which is given to the repentant.

21.1.0.en: "The daughter of Sion": one of the names of Jerusalem.

21.1.1.en: As is the custom of Matthew the Evangelist, he declares that in Christ the prophecies are fulfilled. For Zechariah the prophet prophesied (Zech 9:9) of Christ's entry into Jerusalem in humility and meekness, to reign over hearts, and not as an earthly king, and therefore His procession is simple, riding on weak animals like the ass and the colt.

21.2.0.en: The two disciples of Christ carried out what He commanded them, and brought to Him the ass and the colt, that He might ride on them and enter Jerusalem.

21.3.0.en: Taking off a garment and giving it to another means, in Jewish custom, submission to him as a chief, for a person gives up what is necessary for him in order to submit to the other. And they put them humbly on the animals that Christ would ride, to be blessed by His sitting on them, and they even cast them on the ground for the same reason.

21.3.1.en: Take off your material concerns by fasting and detachment, and you will enjoy the blessing of God to whom you submit, and He will fill you with His grace.

21.4.0.en: The multitude also put their garments on the ground to be blessed, and they cut branches from the trees and spread them in the way, for Him to pass over them on the ass or the colt, so that the ground was clothed with greenness, that is, goodness, because He is the maker of good things.

21.4.1.en: "Branches from the trees": they point to the prophecies that were spoken about Christ, and are now fulfilled in Him. They also point to everything that is lofty, which is at His feet, because He is the Creator of all.

21.5.0.en: All the multitudes who went before Him to spread the way for Him, and who followed Him, declared their faith in Him that He is the awaited Messiah, the son of David, who comes in the name of the Lord to save them.

21.5.1.en: "The multitudes that went before": they point to the men of God in the Old Testament.

21.5.2.en: "And that followed": they signify the faithful in the New Testament, who believed the message of the Gospel, for all seek their salvation in Christ.

21.5.3.en: "Hosanna": its meaning is save us, for He is the Savior who lifts them to the heights in the Kingdom of Heaven. It also comes in the sense of glory.

21.6.0.en: It was a simple popular procession but a mighty one, for hearts were attached to Christ who loved them and cared for them, and the leaders of the city and the priests asked, Who is this procession for? and learned that it is for Jesus the Nazarene who teaches the multitudes, and heals their sicknesses and takes care of them.

21.6.1.en: Be concerned to win the love of others, and not to be raised above them by your position and authority, for all this passes away.

21.7.0.en: Connected with the temple was a group of open halls or courts in which the people gathered. And in them the merchants sold what those coming to the temple needed of animals or birds to offer on the altar.

21.7.1.en: And the Jews from different countries came at the feasts, so the priests arranged for money changers to change currencies into Jewish currency, and they had great financial gain from this trade.

21.7.2.en: And so people's preoccupation turned from concern for worship to buying their needs, and there may have been other goods they sold that had no connection with worship.

21.7.3.en: For if it was necessary to provide some needs related to worship, their sale should be outside all the courts of the temple, so that all the places of the temple remain for worship and teaching.

21.7.4.en: The zeal of Christ for the house of God appeared when He made a scourge (which signifies the Holy Spirit who rebukes us for our preoccupation with material thoughts inside the Church) to drive out with it the animals and birds and the large gatherings for trade inside the temple (Jn 2:15), declaring that the house of God is consecrated for prayer and worship only, as Isaiah said (Isa 56:7), and not for commercial gain, for the priests and their followers had become lovers of money like thieves who steal to heap up much wealth. For by this trade they turned the temple into a cave where thieves gather their material possessions. And Christ drove the sellers out of the temple on Monday, that is, the day after His entry into Jerusalem, but Matthew is not concerned with the order of events.

21.8.0.en: After the cleansing of the temple, there was quiet and an opportunity for spiritual work, so He healed the blind and the lame that they might be enlightened with the knowledge of God and hasten on the way of the spiritual life.

21.8.1.en: And those coming to the temple felt that Christ is the awaited Messiah, and perhaps they had been with Him in the procession of His entry into Jerusalem, so they repeated the acclamations they had said to Him, especially the children among them, who had memorized these phrases from their much repetition, saying: "Hosanna to the Son of David", and the chief priests and scribes were troubled by these acclamations because they are a clear declaration that He is the awaited Messiah, the son of David, as the prophecies said, and they said to Him: "Hearest thou what these say?"

21.8.2.en: Christ answered them with what is written in the prophets they have, that God prepares praise for Himself, which rises from the mouths of children (Ps 8:2).

21.9.0.en: After this, Christ went to the village of Bethany, whose meaning is "house of affliction", and which lies east of Jerusalem, where the house of His friend Lazarus whom He raised from the dead was, and He lodged there to return the next day to Jerusalem.

21.9.1.en: Your heart is the temple of God, so do not let the thoughts of the world occupy it, because God created it in you that prayers may be raised from it. So set aside sufficient time for your prayers before your occupations; and also during your work, lift your heart with short prayers to enjoy fellowship with God.

21.10.0.en: In the morning, Christ set out walking from Bethany, returning to Jerusalem to teach in the temple, and He was hungry, and this is a proof of His humanity. And on the way, He saw from afar a fig tree full of green leaves, so He came to it to eat figs, but when He reached it He found no fruit on it, so He said to it that it would never bear fruit, and it withered and died, and this is a proof of His divinity.

21.10.1.en: It is to be noted that Matthew the Evangelist was not concerned with the order of the time of events like Mark, because the fig tree was cursed by Christ on Monday morning, and the disciples noticed that it had withered on Tuesday morning as Mark the Evangelist mentions (Mk 11:14 and 20), whereas Matthew mentioned the cursing of the fig tree and its withering together.

21.10.2.en: And Christ did this to declare the seriousness of superficiality in the spiritual life, like the Jews who have the appearance of knowing God, but have not the fruits of love for others.

21.10.3.en: And every person who has the appearance of piety but not its depth is rejected by God, and condemned to death, for people come to him to know God, and they find no spiritual fruit in him.

21.10.4.en: "A fig tree": it signifies the Jewish nation and its temple. And because they rejected Christ, the destruction of the temple took place in the year 70 AD. And the withering of the fig tree is a prophecy of the destruction of Jerusalem.

21.10.5.en: And we find that the miracles of Christ declare His mercy, and this is the only miracle that declares the justice of God, so that our view of Him may be complete, and we remember His mercy and His justice at the same time, that we may repent and enjoy His mercies.

21.11.0.en: The disciples marveled at the fig tree's withering at once, so Christ seized this opportunity to show them the power of faith by which they can do everything, even the mountain, they can pluck it from the earth and cast it into the sea, if they have faith.

21.11.1.en: And the mountain points to the many lusts that reign over the heart, so if a person has faith and holds fast to God, he can cast this mountain into the sea, which represents the world, that is, he is rid of worldly lusts. Prayer with faith and persistence gives us everything we ask, on condition that it is in accordance with the will of God. So do not slacken, but ask God with faith for all your needs, and press upon Him, for He loves to hear your voice and give you all good things.

21.12.0.en: The chief priests and elders tried to catch Christ in a fault, because He is not of the tribe of Levi, which is responsible for teaching, but of the tribe of Judah.

21.12.1.en: And since they noticed His driving out of the sellers and the power of His teaching, they asked Him by what authority He teaches and works miracles, and who gave Him permission and allowed Him to do this: was it with the permission of the high priest?

21.12.2.en: They did not ask to know the power of God in Him, but perhaps He would err in some expression, and they would regard Him as breaking the Law and the order of the temple.

21.13.0.en: If the chief priests used human craftiness and cunning, Christ, the true wisdom, answered them with a question, and His intention was not to evade answering, because His question answers them. That is, if they had believed the call of John the Baptist, they would have believed his words about Christ and His authority. And Christ's question was about the source of John's baptism: was it from heaven, and God sent him, or from men, that is, a mere human claim?

21.13.1.en: So they reasoned among themselves, if they admitted that it was from God, He would ask them why they did not believe him and were not baptized by his hands? And if they declared their rejection of his baptism, they feared the people, because all knew that he was a great prophet, so they said: "We cannot tell", that is, their inability to answer appeared, because they feared declaring their true opinion, which was their rejection of John, for fear for their position and authority, and their unreadiness to repent. So Christ said to them: Neither tell I you by what authority I do these things.

21.13.2.en: And so He silenced them so that they would stop trying to catch Him in a fault, and would turn to their weakness, and mend it by accepting the call of John the Baptist, that is, repentance from their sins.

21.13.3.en: Do not be biased in your speech with others, but look for what benefits you, and learn from everyone, and offer love to all.

21.14.s.en: (5) The parable of the two sons and the vineyard

21.14.0.en: The vineyard: it is the opportunity of life on earth in which we strive in holy worship of God, or waste it in the lusts of the world.

21.14.1.en: In the face of the refusal of the chief priests and elders to repent at the call of John or at the preaching of Christ, He gave them a parable about a father, who is God, who had two sons:

21.14.2.en: The first son: he signifies the Gentiles who refused to work with Him in His vineyard, that is, the Church, but afterward repented and worked in the vineyard. He also signifies the tax collectors and sinners who lived their lives far from God, but believed in Christ and repented and became saints.

21.14.3.en: The second son: he signifies the Jews or the scribes and Pharisees, who declared in words their submission to God and their following of Him, but refused to live with Him, that is, to believe in Christ and cleave to His Church.

21.15.0.en: Then Christ asked: Whether of them twain did the will of his father? They said: The first. So He declared to them clearly that those far from God, like the tax collectors and harlots, that is, those immersed in every sin, can believe and repent, and so precede into the Kingdom those who call themselves believers, like the Jews, but do not do the will of God in love and doing good. So the far ones are the true children of the Church, that is, they are the believers in Christ, and not the rejecting Jews.

21.15.1.en: "In the way of righteousness": John the Baptist declared to you the truth of the necessity of repentance and returning to God.

21.15.2.en: "Ye repented not afterward": that is, you are still insisting on not repenting, content with formal worship, and your hearts are evil.

21.15.3.en: If God calls you to repentance through the Holy Bible or the teachings of the Church, or by any remark from those around you, or through the events of life, do not postpone your return to God, and do not promise Him with your mouth, then become occupied away from Him with the circumstances of life, but hasten to your father of confession, and partake of the Holy Mysteries to receive strength, and begin your spiritual striving and fellowship with God.

21.16.0.en: Christ summed up the history of the Jewish nation in this parable.

21.16.1.en: "An householder": he is God who planted a vineyard, that is, the people of the Jews, the descendants of Abraham, and hedged it round about, that is, the commandments and the Law by the hand of Moses.

21.16.2.en: "A winepress": it is the enduring of sufferings for the sake of holding fast to the word of God and serving Him, which the Jews were unable to do, so Christ completed it by His cross, and trod the winepress alone (Isa 63:3).

21.16.3.en: "A tower": the leaders of the people and its elders, responsible for watching over the people and the attacks of enemies from above the tower, to warn them of that. And they include the heads of the tribes and clans and the teachers and all the leaders of the people. "Husbandmen": they are the priests of the Jews responsible for the care of the planted vineyard so that it may bear holy fruits, that is, virtues and a pure life, in the hearts of the believing Jews.

21.16.4.en: "And went into a far country": that is, after He had revealed Himself clearly like a great fire on the mountain in the days of Moses, and the fathers Abraham, Isaac and Jacob, He disappeared from the eyes of the people because of their absorption in sins, so they no longer saw Him, as though He had traveled.

21.17.0.en: "His servants": whom He sent to receive the fruits, and they are the prophets and men of God sent to His people throughout history, to reap a life full of virtues from the believing Jews, but sadly the priests of the Jews and their leaders opposed them and tortured them, and scourged some, killed some, and stoned some, that is, they rejected their teachings which are the voice of God to them.

21.17.1.en: And God lengthened His forbearance (patience) toward them, by sending other servants also, more than the first, that is, a great number of prophets, and the priests opposed them and rejected them like the first.

21.18.0.en: The last opportunity and the greatest work that God offered to the Jewish people is the incarnation of His only Son, as was told them in the prophecies of the prophets, to save them.

21.18.1.en: And in the parable, the husbandmen knew that he was the son of the owner of the vineyard and the heir of all that is in it, so instead of submitting to him and giving him the fruits, they rose against him and killed him.

21.18.2.en: And the chief priests, for their purposes of chief place and material things, refused to understand that Jesus is the awaited Messiah. And instead of believing in Him, they opposed Him lest He take their position, and they crucified Him on the cross. And so pride and the love of chief place appear, which blinded the eyes of the priests, to the point of rejecting the awaited Messiah, the Son of God.

21.19.0.en: Christ asked the scribes and Pharisees who were listening to Him about the fitting action of the owner of the vineyard toward the wicked husbandmen, and they said to Him: He will destroy them, and let out the vineyard to other husbandmen better than they, who will render him the fruits in their seasons.

21.19.1.en: This is the fate of the priests of the Jews who refuse to believe in Christ, that is, eternal torment.

21.19.2.en: "Other husbandmen": the disciples and Apostles and the Christian priesthood.

21.20.0.en: "The stone": it is Christ, and the building is the Church, and the chief builder who chose this stone is God.

21.20.1.en: "Marvellous in our eyes": according to the limited human view, Christ appears to be from a humble family, and has no wealth or material position, but He is God who humbled Himself for our salvation, and we need faith to receive Him.

21.20.2.en: Christ reminded them of what is written in (Ps 118:22) about the stone that the builders think useless, and then discover in the end that it is the most suitable stone to be the head of the corner, that is, joining the two walls together. And this stone signifies Christ the Savior of the Jews and the Gentiles, for He is the One whom God sent, and the priests did not understand that.

21.20.3.en: And Christ states clearly to the chief priests that the Kingdom of God which He promised His people will be taken from them because of their unbelief, and given to the Gentiles who believe in Him, and He means that the unbelieving Jews will be replaced in the Church of Christ by the believers from the Gentiles.

21.20.4.en: And whoever opposes Christ falls on the stone to break it, and he is himself bruised, that is, he meets troubles.

21.20.5.en: But if he repents and believes, God receives him.

21.20.6.en: But whoever remains refusing to believe in Him, He will judge him in the end and condemn him to destruction, that is, the stone will fall on him and grind him to powder.

21.21.0.en: The chief priests and Pharisees understood that the parable was about them, and instead of repenting, they were enraged at it and tried to arrest Him, but they feared the people, because in their view He was a great prophet. If others expose your faults to you, do not resist them, but hasten to repentance, for their words are a message from God. The parable of the wedding, the beliefs of the Sadducees, the greatest commandment
